_note: MC2-05-BRIGHTEN-1 (supersedes BUILDING-FACE-POSE-1's version of this file). mc2_05 non-degradation set; its night lighting is USER-APPROVED so prop-lighting changes must be shown not to damage it. Sites are building-class object clusters read out of the mission .pak packet-1 object list and classified by ObjectTypeClass (method note in mc2_10_building_faces.json): 'refinery' = the 34-object plant at (-1006,4587); 'east_compound' = the 82-object walled compound at (3133,-1788). Sun azimuth = LightDirYaw(15)+45 = 60 deg, so rot 60 frames the lit faces and rot 240 the faces turned away. The control frames terrain carrying no building-class object. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE PREVIOUS VERSION OF THIS FILE, both measured. (1) The 'liao_compound' poses at (-4009,-2751) ARE REMOVED. They were recorded as having a 0.000 percent gate-OFF/gate-OFF noise floor; they do not. Two identical gate-OFF runs of liao_compound_lightaway differ on 15.0 percent of pixels at maxAbs 28 (lightfacing 14.8 percent / 29). The unstable region is a smooth radial night LIGHT POOL in the upper right of the frame, and it is unstable because object light pools are dimmed near movers (MC2_LIGHT_POOL_MOVER_DIM, default 0.25, gos_terrain_lighting.cpp:651) while movers do not resolve to the same position twice. The gate-ON arm is worse still and is the decisive receipt: two runs with IDENTICAL settings (gate 0.55, pools default) differ on 46.4 percent of pixels at maxAbs 82, with 30.1 percent of pixels brighter and mean luminance swinging 87.50 to 94.14 -- a 6.64 luminance run-to-run swing, LARGER than the entire +7.4 luminance effect that was reported as the brightening blocker. Re-running the same A/B with MC2_TERRAIN_LIGHT_POOLS=0 collapses all of it: gate-OFF vs gate-OFF and gate-ON vs gate-ON both go byte-identical (0.000 percent, maxAbs 0) and the gate effect resolves to a clean -0.33 mean luminance with 0.00 percent of pixels brighter. The pose was therefore measuring mover positions, not lighting. This is the same class of defect that got the LiaoSpotlight yard pose at (-236,448) removed from the previous version (84-91 percent floor, animated cone glow) and it is removed for the same reason: a pose whose noise floor exceeds the effect being graded cannot grade anything, and it would flap the determinism ratchet. A false 0.000 percent floor on these two poses is what produced the reported 'MC2_PROP_BASE_LIGHT_DIR brightens mc2_05 by up to +71 percent' blocker, which does not reproduce once the pose is stabilised. (2) The previous note claimed mc2_05 'is the only tier map that runs a real day/night cycle'. mc2_05 does carry DayToNightTime=864000 where the other tier maps carry -1, but THERE IS NO RUNTIME CYCLE ON ANY MAP: Camera::update's per-frame updateDaylight() call is commented out (mclib/camera.cpp:2180, 'WE ARE NEVER TRANSITIONING ANYMORE') and updateDaylight is only ever called once with bInitialize=true (camera.cpp:2766). nightFactor is a per-mission constant, and the cycle claim must not be reused as a distinguishing condition. KNOWN GAP, recorded rather than hidden: the LiaoSpotlight fixtures ARE part of the approved night look and remain ungradeable until a stable pose exists for them; the compounds around them are covered here.
